source.title: Humans monitor learning progress in curiosity-driven exploration.

confidence_rationale: Human free-choice data: when people choose freely among learning activities, models with a learning-progress term fit task selection best, and people avoid unlearnable activities while taking on hard learnable ones. That is the anti-randomness discriminator of ARC-136 measured in humans. Adult lab task, not play or development, so held at 0.70.
failure_signatures: Participants were adults doing a short, instructed free-choice task; this shows learning progress guides voluntary task choice, not that it produces spontaneous play or a developmental curriculum.
People also used competence (percent correct) to avoid easy tasks, so exploration is not driven by learning progress alone; a pure learning-progress model is not the best fit either.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a free-choice paradigm with several learning activities of differing learnability, humans' task selection is best fit by models that include a learning-progress component alongside competence; people avoid tasks that are too easy and avoid laboring on unlearnable tasks while still self-challenging on difficult learnable ones.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct human evidence for ARC-136 leg (1)'s discriminator: sampling is drawn to LEARNABLE uncertainty and away from unlearnable (stochastic) activities, not simply to the most uncertain option. An REE intrinsic drive of the epistemic-deficit or raw-novelty type would fail this test; a learning-progress term passes it.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Adult, instructed, lab-based; no viability or commitment context. It evidences the drive's selection rule, not play's developmental emergence or migration across affordance spaces.
mapping.source_context: Human online free-choice experiment with four learning activities of varying difficulty (one unlearnable); computational model comparison of intrinsic utility functions.

confidence_components.notes: Well-designed, pre-specified model comparison in a strong journal; mapping is to the selection rule, not play itself.
